systematic_findings: POST-CHECK (DOI title check) drops correct DOIs: all 4 wave-7 drops are the right record (GusmEtal14: ®/™ vs {\textregistered}/{\texttrademark}; HernEtal00: Crossref HTML tags glued to words, 'D<sub>2</sub>Dopamine', 'Ca<sup>2+</sup>Currents'; LismIdia95: '7 ± 2' vs '$7\pm2$'; Rebe10: generic column title 'Ask the Brains' with volume, issue and page equal to the entry's). Suggest: strip HTML tags as separators, map \pm/\textregistered/\texttrademark to their Unicode forms, and accept (or hold instead of drop) a generic registry title when first page + volume + issue + year match.

POST-CHECK (quote failure + removal): when the researcher's booktitle fails its quote check ('ieee' not in the CVF quote), the booktitle is dropped but the researcher's journal removal is still honoured, so GatyEtal16, IsolEtal17 and LiEtal24a end as @inproceedings with NO venue (the only 3 such rows among all 400). A contained type should never lose its last venue: keep the journal as booktitle, or hold the booktitle as unverified-but-kept.

POST-CHECK (surname hold) keeps obvious misspellings when a second host exists but was not quoted: CaliVita05 'Calibrasi' (Crossref and arXiv cs/0412098 both 'Cilibrasi'; the key should then be CiliVita07, not CaliVita07) and ChanEtal20 'Geerlings' (DataCite 'Geerligs'). The hold also drives the key rename, so a held misspelling gets baked into a new key.

POST-CHECK (needs_user): replacement candidates written in the researcher's notes are not surfaced when nothing else flags the row: TsitEtal19 (Crossref is-preprint-of 10.1016/j.cub.2019.11.048), LiEtal24b and JainHuth18 have needs_user=false, so the user's per-entry preprint->published decision is skipped.
